key_insight: A hybrid unstructured mesh can be locally refined around immersed geometries to make immersed boundary simulations more accurate and efficient without requiring a fully body-fitted mesh everywhere.
engineering_relevance: This enables practical CFD workflows for configurations with fixed and moving parts, such as airfoils and multi-element wings, where only the changing geometry needs immersed treatment.
method: Input: conforming hybrid background mesh from external mesher (tetrahedra, hexahedra, prisms, pyramids).
Adapt/refine the mesh around immersed bodies to support immersed boundary CFD solvers.
Validate on subsonic cylinder, NACA0012, and a multi-element airfoil using FV and DG with Navier–Stokes/RANS.
evidence_signal: The adapted meshes produced simulation results that were reported to agree well with experimental data across the test cases.
watch_item: Performance and accuracy depend on the quality of the initial hybrid mesh and careful refinement near the immersed surface to avoid degraded solver behavior.
paper_title: Mesh Adaptation on Hybrid Unstructured Meshes for Immersed Boundary Methods
